Separately, NYC's pied-a-terre/second-home tax, projected to raise $500M annually, faces a temporary judicial pause after a Staten Island homeowners lawsuit, while Trump says he is exploring a federal block of the tax. A federal judge has also paused the Trump administration's suspension of LA homelessness funds. A federal judge warned the Trump DOJ it could be held in contempt over withheld and unredacted Epstein files, calling it a promise not a threat at a public hearing; and the Trump DOJ has separately moved to have a judge removed from an IRS case, with reports of alleged DOJ coordination on a Trump appeal. New development: the DOJ is appealing a May ruling by Judge Waverly Crenshaw that dismissed human smuggling charges against Kilmar Abrego Garcia, a Salvadoran national wrongfully deported to El Salvador, after the court found the prosecution was vindictive; Abrego Garcia's attorneys say the DOJ's appeal is unfounded.
